title: Axonemal regulation by curvature explains sperm flagellar waveform modulation
authors: Gallagher MT; Kirkman-Brown JC; Smith DJ
one_liner_zh: 该文研究精子鞭毛弯曲调控的力学模型，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，与课题无关。
abstract: Flagellar motility is critical to natural and many forms of assisted reproduction. The rhythmic beating and wave propagation by the flagellum propels sperm through fluid and enables modulation between penetrative progressive motion, activated side-to-side yaw and hyperactivated movement associated with detachment from epithelial binding. These changes occur in response to the properties of the surrounding fluid environment, biochemical activation state, and physiological ligands, however a parsimonious mechanistic explanation of flagellar beat generation that can explain motility modulation is lacking. In this paper we present the Axonemal Regulation of Curvature, Hysteretic model (ARCH), a curvature control-type model based on switching of active moment by local curvature, embedded within a geometrically nonlinear elastic model of the flagellum exhibiting planar flagellar beats, together with nonlocal viscous fluid dynamics. The biophysical system is parameterised completely by four dimensionless parameter groupings. The effect of parameter variation is explored through computational simulation, revealing beat patterns that are qualitatively representative of penetrative (straight progressive), activated (highly yawing) and hyperactivated (non-progressive) modes. Analysis of the flagellar limit cycles and associated swimming velocity reveals a cusp catastrophe between progressive and non-progressive modes, and hysteresis in the response to changes in critical curvature parameter. Quantitative comparison to experimental data on human sperm exhibiting typical penetrative, activated and hyperactivated beats shows a good fit to the time-average absolute curvature profile along the flagellum, providing evidence that the model is capable of providing a framework for quantitative interpretation of imaging data.
abstract_zh: 鞭毛运动对自然生殖及多种辅助生殖方式至关重要。鞭毛的节律性拍打和波传播推动精子穿过液体，并使其能够在穿透性前进运动、激活的侧向偏航运动以及与上皮结合脱离相关的超激活运动之间进行调节。这些变化响应于周围液体环境的特性、生化激活状态和生理配体而发生，然而，缺乏一种能够解释运动调节的鞭毛拍打生成的简约机制性解释。本文提出了曲率轴丝调节滞回模型（Axonemal Regulation of Curvature, Hysteretic model, ARCH），这是一种基于局部曲率切换主动力矩的曲率控制型模型，嵌入在展示平面鞭毛拍打的几何非线性弹性鞭毛模型中，并结合非局部粘性流体动力学。该生物物理系统完全由四个无量纲参数组参数化。通过计算模拟探索参数变化的影响，揭示出定性代表穿透性（直线前进）、激活（高偏航）和超激活（非前进）模式的拍打模式。对鞭毛极限环及相关游泳速度的分析揭示了前进与非前进模式之间的尖点突变，以及对临界曲率参数变化的滞回响应。与展示典型穿透性、激活和超激活拍打的人类精子实验数据的定量比较显示，沿鞭毛的时间平均绝对曲率分布拟合良好，为模型能够提供成像数据定量解释框架提供了证据。
